title: Shortlister score-dispersion gating + lightweight locale adapters for hybrid rerank selection
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: reduce downstream rerank latency and regression risk while preserving or improving quality for long-tail locales. Approach: introduce a shortlister-score-dispersion gating policy that decides between calling a full cross-encoder vs a lightweight locale-conditioned adapter rescorer. The gate uses statistics over the shortlister candidate scores (e.g., score variance, top-1 - top-5 gap, entropy) together with request locale and document-language signals to select the path. This lets us avoid expensive cross-encoder calls for low-variance ranking problems and apply focused lightweight adapters for locale-specific failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: P99 end-to-end rerank latency reduction >= 20% for high-throughput tail traffic compared to baseline cross-encoder-only path
MRR@10 and nDCG@10 regressions <= 0.5% on global English + staging multilingual eval sets
Automated smoke-suite detects none of the high-severity multilingual regressions during canary (see smoke tests list)
Canary rollout with automated rollback threshold (quality drop > 1% or P99 latency increase > 10%) succeeds in 4 regional cohorts
planned_workflow: Week 1: offline analysis of shortlister score distributions across top 50 locales; derive candidate gating thresholds and features
Week 2: implement gating service in rerank router (feature-flagged). Implement lightweight locale adapter model (quantized 8-bit distilled transformer) and optimized batching for adapter path
Week 3: integrate smoke/regression harness, build localized eval suites for 12 priority long-tail locales, and add KV warmstart for adapter path
Week 4: staging canary (10% traffic split by synthetic cohorts), collect metrics for 48h, run automatic rollback checks, iterate on thresholds
Week 5: progressive rollout with regional cohorts and final runbook for Dedicated customers
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Design choice: gating at router vs inside model ensemble. Router gating reduces wasted cross-encoder KV cache pressure but requires quick, low-latency decision logic (adds ~1-2ms). We chose router gating to simplify per-request routing and to keep model-specific telemetry aligned with invocation counts.

Adapter model scope: to minimize regression surface, adapter acts on embedding + shortlister top-k context (k=16) and outputs pairwise deltas. This is cheaper than a full cross-encoder but may miss fine-grained interactions; we will retain cross-encoder fallback for high-entropy candidates.
Quantization: adapter will be 8-bit quantized to meet latency SLOs; tradeoff is slightly lower absolute quality on some morphologically rich languages — we will tune per-locale adapters where needed.
Complexity vs observability: added gate increases routing pathways. We've prioritized rich telemetry (gate_reason, dispersion_metrics, fallback_counts) to make regressions diagnosable quickly.
implementation_notes: Schema changes: add 'gate_reason' and 'shortlister_stats' to rerank request logs; update console dashboards to surface gate hit-rate by model variant and locale
Batching: implement per-path batching windows (cross-encoder: 10ms continuous batching; adapter path: 4ms micro-batches) to balance latency and throughput
KV cache: adapter path reuses shortlister embeddings; ensure we don't evict cross-encoder KV entries prematurely — adjust eviction policy to LRU with model-tag awareness
Testing: unit tests for gating logic, integration tests for routing, and a new multilingual smoke suite that includes synthetic adversarial pairs for 18 target locales
updates: 2026-02-22: Ran offline analysis of 1M shortlister responses. Observed that 42% of requests have top-5 score stddev < 0.03 (good candidates for adapter path). Aisha: "Initial thresholds: stddev < 0.03 && top1-top5_gap < 0.08 -> adapter_path"

2026-02-27: Prototype routing change merged to feature branch. Early micro-benchmarks show adapter inference P95 latency 12ms (on CPU-pool) vs cross-encoder 48ms (GPU). Marco: preparing smoke harness for staging

2026-03-03: First multilingual eval: adapter-only on Portuguese-PT showed MRR@10 drop of 1.8% vs baseline. Investigation: adapter lacks morphological cues. Decision: add locale-conditioned byte-level tokenizer and retrain PT adapter. Adding PT to high-priority locale list
2026-03-08: Implemented gate telemetry fields and dashboard draft. QA found missing correlation id propagation for adapter path; patch in PR #4132 addressing tracing header forwarding

2026-03-11: Staging canary rollout (5% synthetic traffic) started. After 12h, overall P99 latency down 23%, global MRR@10 change +0.1%. Two locales (pt-PT, ru-RU) flagged for manual review (PT quality -1.2%, RU adapter instability). Rolling back adapter for RU cohort and continuing PT retrain
review_feedback: PM Product: request adding a conservative fallback policy where any adapter-confident-score delta below threshold triggers cross-encoder verification for first N requests per user (to catch distribution shifts)
Design: suggest adding a UX telemetry tag for end-to-end user-visible latency buckets to correlate perceived latency with technical metrics
Infra: ask to include resource isolation constraints for Dedicated pools; adapter path should default to tenant-shared CPU pool unless tenant opts into Dedicated adapters
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: adapter introduces subtle regressions in morphologically-rich languages — Mitigation: per-locale adapter retrain and conservative canary thresholds

Risk: gating logic misfires under distribution shift (e.g., sudden spike in long-tail query types) — Mitigation: maintain cross-encoder budget and automatic fallback when gate_hit_rate changes > 10%/hour
Risk: telemetry volume increases (gate_reason + stats) — Mitigation: sampling at 1% for full payloads with aggregated counters at 100%
